variants: Sringeri; Shringeri; Sringéri; Srngeri; Sringagiri; Sringa-giri; Rishya-Sringa-giri; Sringiri; Shringori
note: Seat of the Jagadguru, 'proprietor of the surrounding tract'; jāgīr of about 9,144 people granted 1346; revenue c. Rs 50,000 plus Rs 1,000 a month from Mysore (Rice 1876, 1897). Located in no Bombay or Madras Places chapter. Rivals: Liṅgāyats (Kanara's Konkan Kuṇbīs left 'the Lingayat guide of Chitaldurg' for Śṛṅgeri in 1881; Bellary procession dispute 1888; Liṅgāyat conches allowed in Śṛṅgeri's processions); Mādhvas (Uḍupi; Uttarādi and Ahobila complaints 1906–07; Srirangapatna 1895; Vyāsarāja's claim to equal honours 1931); the Havig gurus (Svarṇavallī, Rāmacandrapura); and the seats that separated from it, Saṅkeśvar and Kudli, which held the Bombay Karnatak estates.

name: Saṅkeśvar
note: Seat of the Saṅkeśvar Svāmī: 30 inām villages in seven jurisdictions, Rs 30,000 a year; told as a secession from Śṛṅgeri c. 1570 (Belgaum 1884, pp. 600–02). Its villages lie mainly in Kolhapur, Belgaum and the Maratha states; those of its neighbour Kudli (Kudalgi), the first maṭh of its origin story, lie mainly in Dharwar and Bijapur (30 taluks and states in the 1934 list; 'Kudli estates' filter). A Bombay officer (1896) recommended exempting the Kudalgi Svāmī from the Arms Act like his 'brother Swami of Sankeshwar … in no way superior in position'. Rivals: a Saṅkeśvar nominee challenged Śṛṅgeri's accredited agent in Khandesh (1913, Mysore files).

name: Kudli
variants: Kudali; Kūḍali; Kudalgi; Kudli Sringeri Matt; Uddughatti Mutt
note: Confluence of the Tunga and Bhadra. A Smārta maṭh whose guru was appointed by Śṛṅgeri (Rice) or founded by the Saṅkeśvar secessionist (Belgaum). Mysore files: 'a separate branch … at the Partition of A. D. 1656-57'; income Rs 35,047 (1933), of which villages and lands outside Mysore brought Rs 16,798 and those inside Rs 5,594. Estates (Agent's list, March 1934): Dharwar (Ranibennur, Karajgi, Hangal, Kod, Shiggaon, Navalgund, Kalghatgi, Dharwar, Hubli, Ron, Gadag); Bijapur (Badami, Bagalkot, Bagevadi, Bijapur, Sindgi, Hungund); Belgaum (Parasgad); North Kanara (Mundgod); Bellary (Kudligi, Harapanahalli); Anantapur (Madakasira); Kolhapur (Torgal), Ramdurg, Sangli (Shirahatti), Miraj Senior (Lakshmeshwar), Miraj Junior (Gudageri), Savanur, Sirasangi, Jamkhandi (Kundgol). Bombay levied nazarana on the Dharwar and Bijapur ināms (Rs 2,745 and Rs 1,167, 1936) and calls the maṭh 'Kudalgi' or the 'Uddughatti Mutt'. Use the 'Kudli estates' filter to see them. Also a Mādhva maṭh (Akṣobhya Tīrtha). Rivals: Liṅgāyat objections were feared when its Svāmī was allowed the ambari (1931); a rival line of claimants was rejected 1875–1929; the Mādhva Akṣobhya Tīrtha maṭh stands in the same village.

name: Dvārkā
variants: Dwarka; Dwarika; Dwárka; Sharada Pith; Shārada Pīth
note: 'Shārada Pīth … endowed by the Gaekwar of Baroda, who sanctions the appointment of every new pontiff' (Gujarat 1901, p. 542). Rivals: in Vaiṣṇava Gujarat (Vallabha, Svāminārāyaṇa) its pontiff is referee only for the 'Śaivas'.

name: Jyotirmaṭh
note: Named in lists of the four maṭhs; 'established the Joshimath monastery' (Garhwal 1910). Place entries describe only the Badrinath Rawal's winter seat.

name: Badrinath
note: Temple 'said to have been erected … by Sankara Acharya'; Nambūri Rawal from Malabar; estates of 164 villages and parts of 111 (1910). Rivals: its Rawal is a Nambūri from Malabar; Kedarnath and Ukhimath are described as a Jangama (Liṅgāyat) maṭh (Atkinson; Garhwal 1910).

name: Kumbakoṇam
note: 'the math of Sankaracharya', income nearly Rs 14,000, appoints the managers of three temples incl. one at Conjeeveram (Tanjore 1906). Catalogued as 'Kanchi Komakoti matt at Kumbakonam' in 1925. Rivals: Tanjore's list of chief maṭhs (1906) names the non-Brahmin Śaiva maṭhs of Dharmapuram, Tiruvāvaḍuturai, Tiruppanandāl and Tiruppugalūr first; the Vaḍagalai Ahobila maṭh had moved to Narasimhapuram nearby (Thurston).

name: Kāñcī
note: Where Śaṅkara 'founded a matam' (Crole 1879, p. 26); a temple managed from Kumbakoṇam (1906); the maṭh is 'of Conjeevaram' by 1936.

name: Purī (Govardhana maṭha)
note: Absent in 1877; 'the Sankaracharya' maṭh with c. 1,200 MSS (1908); 'Gobardhana Matha … still extant' (1977). A Kāñcī Kāmakoṭi ashram founded at Purī in 1973. Rivals: the town's 70-odd maṭhs are mostly Vaiṣṇava foundations (Emār, Rāghavadāsa and others). Rivals (coded): 29 Purī maṭhs drew Rs 1,45,400 a year from land in 1848; Śaṅkara-line houses are about 7 of some 130 in 1977.

name: Śivagaṅgā
note: Maṭh in financial difficulty, endowments under Muzrai management at the guru's wish (Rice 1897); funds lent for the Śṛṅgeri Jagadguru's visit (1927).

name: Avani
note: 'A guru of the Smarta sect resides here' (Rice 1876, 1897); a Śaṅkarācārya temple with a State grant (1930); 'Avani Sringeri Mutt' (1933).

name: Hampi
variants: Virupaksha; Virūpākṣa; Pampa; Pampapati; Hampi Samsthanam
note: Sri Sankaracharya Virupaksha Samsthanam: its Svāmī calls it 'a branch of Sri Sringeri Mutt', papers 'left behind in the Nizam's Dominions' (Mysore file, 1935–36). No maṭh in the Bellary volumes. Rivals: put forward as a rival seat to Śṛṅgeri at the 1912 succession (Mysore files).

name: Puṣpagiri
note: Temple hill and hamlet of Kotlur in the Cuddapah volumes; no maṭh described, and no archival file found.

name: Khidrapur
note: 'an alienated village belonging to Sankeshvar Svami' (Kolhapur 1886, p. 302).

name: Hallur
note: Rangnath temple rebuilt by the Kudalgi Svāmī, who was granted the village (Dharwar 1884, p. 722).

name: Hubli
note: Kudalgi Svāmī's crosswise-palkhi privilege upheld up to the Privy Council (Dharwar 1884, p. 757); Hubli taluk is in the Kudli maṭh's 1934 property list. (The 1923 'Hubli Sringeri Matt' file is really about Kudli.) Rivals: the Liṅgāyat Mursavirad Svāmī imitated the Kudalgi Svāmī's crosswise palkhi; the dispute went up to the Privy Council (Dharwar 1884, p. 757).

name: Nirmal
note: Reputed samādhi of a Śaṅkarācārya; temple of Shankaracharya Svāmī built after 1739, Government grant Rs 421 (Thana 1882).

name: Sonda
variants: Sonda; Sunda; Swadi; Svarnavalli; Honalli Math
note: Honalli (Svarṇavallī) Smārta maṭh, seat of the Havig Brahmans' guru: a separate line, not a Śṛṅgeri branch (Kanara 1883). Rivals: the Vaiṣṇava Terbidi (Vādirāja) maṭh stands beside the Svarṇavallī maṭh at Sonda (Kanara 1883).

name: Bodh Gayā
variants: Bodh Gaya; Buddh Gaya; Budh Gaya
note: Giri maṭh, 'one of the seven Saivite orders established by Sankara Acharya' (Gaya 1906); Mahabodhi dispute. Rivals: the Mahabodhi Society (Buddhist) contested the Mahant's possession of the temple; the High Court found for the Mahant (1906).

name: Tārakeśvar
note: Mahant 'a celibate of the Dasnami order'; a public endowment after 1924; 'governed by the Sankaracharya school of thought' (1972). Rivals: Bengal proper is a Vaiṣṇava landscape; Sannyāsīs number in the tens per district against tens of thousands of caste-rejecting Vaiṣṇavas (Hunter, 1872).

name: Bhot-Bagān
note: Tashi Lama's grant to Puran Gir Gosāin (1785); mahant elected 'by the other Dasnami Mahants of Bengal' (1905). Rivals: Bengal proper is a Vaiṣṇava landscape; Sannyāsīs number in the tens per district against tens of thousands of caste-rejecting Vaiṣṇavas (Hunter, 1872).

name: Hardwar
note: Kumbh melā; Kankhal Gosāins (Bhola Gir, 4,024 acres); a Śṛṅgeri maṭh building at Haridwar (Mysore file, 1944). Rivals: the Gosāin–Bairāgī battle at Hardwar, 1760; precedence among Daśanāmī, Bairāgī and Udāsī akhāṛās at the Kumbh.

name: Bodhan
note: One of four monasteries of Bhāskarācārya, the Komaṭis' 'deputy of Shankaracharya' (Sholapur 1884).

name: Nander
note: Another of Bhāskarācārya's monasteries (Sholapur 1884).

name: Khanapur
note: 'The Smart svami has a monastery at Khanapur', with two villages: the Shenvi Smārta svāmī (Belgaum 1884, p. 91).

name: Kollur
note: Mūkāmbikā temple; image said to have been consecrated by Śaṅkara (South Kanara 1973).

name: Karkal
note: An image 'installed at Karkal by Shree Jagadguru Narasimha Bharati Swamiji of Sringeri Matha' (1973).

name: Kaladi
note: Śaṅkara's birthplace (Atkinson spells it 'Kallady'); the Śṛṅgeri Jagadguru's escort from Mysore to Kaladi (1923).

name: Rāmeśvaram
note: A Śṛṅgeri branch maṭh, named in a 1935 Mysore file on legacies.

name: Tirupati
note: Śṛṅgeri maṭh branch at Tirupati, managed by committees (1940). Rivals: the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams claim oversight of the Śṛṅgeri branch because they pay its allowances (1940).

name: Bangalore (Sultanpet)
note: 'Sringeri Matt, Sultanpet, Bangalore city' (1923); the Jagadguru's processions in the city (1907).

name: Mysore
note: Capital of the princely state whose Muzrai files record the Śṛṅgeri and Kudli maṭhs. Rivals: the Ahobila maṭh complained of the Śṛṅgeri Svāmī passing in procession before it (1907).

name: Sangli
note: Kudli Śṛṅgeri maṭh properties in Sangli State (1935).

name: Hole Narsipur
note: The Śṛṅgeri Svāmī's visits (1892) and an adda-palakki dispute in front of the Uttarādi maṭh (1906).

name: Srirangapatna
note: Visits of the Śṛṅgeri Svāmī to the Ranganātha temple (1894–95, 1907).

name: Nanjangud
note: The Śṛṅgeri Jagadguru's endowments to the Śrīkaṇṭheśvara temple (1892, 1907).

name: Kigga
note: Ṛṣyaśṛṅga temple, in the Śṛṅgeri jāgīr.

name: Belavadi
note: An inām village of the Śṛṅgeri maṭh (tank, quarry, land disposals 1902–40).

name: Ayodhyā
note: Dominated by the Bairāgī akhāṛās; the Gosāins appear only in the story of their expulsion from Hanumāngaṛhī. The Rāmānandī Bairāgīs were the Daśanāmīs' direct rival in the north. Rivals (coded): Hanumāngaṛhī's Nirbānī akhāṛā had 300–400 resident disciples (1877), 250 (1905), at most 200 (1960), but grew richer; the Gosāins' expulsion from it is told only in 1960.

name: Gokarn
note: Pilgrimage centre of Kanara castes; earlier seat of the Havig gurus' line before Sonda.

name: Udagatti
note: Where the Kudli svāmīs lived in the Bombay country; Bombay records call the maṭh 'Kudalgi' or the 'Uddughatti Mutt' (Mysore files, 1936).

name: Tīrthamuttūr
note: 'a vassal Mutt to the Sringeri Mutt, paying an annual subsidy of Rs 31-4-0'; its svāmīs consecrated at Śṛṅgeri (1923).

note: Rival centre: the great Kālī pilgrimage of the Calcutta region (24 Parganas 1914).

name: Khardah
note: Rival centre: 'a favourite place of pilgrimage for Vaishnavas, as it was the home of Nityananda' (24 Parganas 1914).

name: Dakshineswar
note: Rani Rasmani's temples to Kālī and Kṛṣṇa with twelve Śiva shrines; the 1914 gazetteer does not mention Ramakrishna, whose order (Belur Math, 1898) took Daśanāmī sannyāsa.

name: Uḍupi
note: Rival centre: seat of the Mādhva maṭhs; Kanara and South Canara Vaiṣṇava Brahmans' guru is 'a Tulu Brahman, who lives in celibacy at the Vaishnav monastery at Udipi'. Rivals: South Canara's largest Tulu Brahman group, the Shivallis (28,660 in 1891), are Mādhva: 'the great bulk of the Tulu Brahmins' (Sturrock 1894).

name: Lormi
note: Rival seat: a Bairāgī estate of 103–104 villages, a Bhonsla grant of 1826 that passed from the chela to his four sons (rivals N-coding). District census 1891 (Bilaspur): Bairāgī 8,647 (Ramanandi 3,804) against Gosain 2,419.

name: Tilla
note: Rival seat: the chief Nāth (Kānphaṭā) monastery of the Punjab, with Akbar's sanad for a jagir, resumed over a murder for the gaddī and later restored (rivals N-coding). District census 1891 (Jhelum): Gosain 10, Sanniasi 76; Jogī-Rawal 1,438 (mostly a caste, not compared: the order's following does not show as a separate heading).

name: Bohar
note: Rival seat: a Kānphaṭā (Nāth) maṭh holding land; Rohtak's 299 asthals on 2,725 acres are half Bairāgī, with the Gosāins fourth (rivals N-coding). District census 1891 (Rohtak): Bairāgī 6,317 against Gosain 568; Jogī-Rawal 3,717 (mostly a caste, not compared).

name: Dera Baba Nanak
note: Rival seat: Udāsī institution with a jagir of Rs 2,602 (rivals N-coding). District census 1891 (Gurdaspur): only 93 Udāsīs returned, against Sanniasi 395 and Gosain 2 (Jogī-Rawal 5,408, mostly a caste, not compared); the seat's following does not show as ascetics.

name: Tiruvāvaḍuturai
note: Rival seat: non-Brahmin Śaiva ādhīnam, about 29,000 acres and Rs 2 lakhs a year, against about Rs 14,000 for the Kumbakoṇam Śaṅkara maṭh (Tanjore 1906; rivals S-coding).

name: Dharmapuram
note: Rival seat: non-Brahmin Śaiva ādhīnam; about 2,500 acres and 27 temples; among the 'Sudra maths' listed first in Tanjore's chief maṭhs (1906). Nearby Tiruppanandāḷ (Rs 80,000 a year) was held independent of it in court.

name: Chitradurga
note: Rival seat: the Murugha maṭh, supreme guru of the Liṅgāyats; Kanara's 14,812 Konkan Kuṇbīs left 'the Lingayat guide of Chitaldurg' for Śṛṅgeri in 1881; the hill maṭh stood deserted owing to 'the opposition of other sects' (rivals S-coding).

name: Vadtal
note: Rival seat: one of the two Svāminārāyaṇa seats; feeds 500–1,000 inmates and draws 20,000 pilgrims a festival; Svāminārāyaṇs 287,687 in 1901 (rivals S-coding).
